title: THE FIRST WORLD
now: Pacing the road to the Ascension, so every village feels earned without the middle dragging.
Making Ora's guidance clear at a glance: one goal, one soft light, never a wall of words.
Vexahl's moves: easy to read, fair to counter, and a little unsettling.
Villages joining family by family: making each home's moment feel like something.
Smoother frames on laptops and older machines.

releases.title: The road to the Ascension
releases.summary: The island has a story now. Ora walks you from your first village to the last, one goal at a time, and the neighbours wait for you to come to them.

items.t: A new island starts in story mode. Ora names one goal at a time on the road to the Ascension, nudges you gently if you're stuck, and a soft light marks the spot.
Finish the story and free play opens up: no guidance, no clock, and you ascend when you choose.
A neighbour comes to believe one home at a time. Each family that joins lights its windows gold and dances for you, and the village is yours once most of its homes believe.

items.h: Your light grows as you tend
items.t: Every answered prayer, gift and finished dream pushes your light a little further out, and it leans along the road toward the next village.
A village beyond your light dreams of nothing yet. Once your light reaches it, it starts to ask, and its temple only rises with your hand.
His isle sits small and hazy at the sea's edge from the very first moment. Partway along the road he notices you, then makes one move against each village you're winning. Every move can be answered.
When the last temple stands, the Ascension waits one full day while the island stays in tune. A quiet last stretch to enjoy what you built.
Vexahl speaks his lines aloud, and Lumi and Fizz voice their new story lines. Ora answers with the deep hum of a singing bowl.
Dialogue sits at the top centre of the screen, one voice at a time, and the world's glow is a touch softer.

releases.title: The lived-in island
releases.summary: The island got its look: warm golden-hour light, cottages with smoking chimneys, roads between the villages, and a coast worth staring at.

items.t: Warmer light, deeper greens and a soft diorama focus, so the whole island looks like a little world on a table.
Stone footings, timber frames and steep shingled roofs. Lived-in homes glow at dusk and send up chimney smoke.
Worn paths link each village's houses, fields and prayer place, and roads run between the villages.
Sea cliffs, waterfalls, rocky islets, a little jetty and two sailboats bobbing offshore.
Barrels, crates, fences and lanterns; stumps where trees fell; gulls circling; cloud shadows drifting over the hills.
Set a villager down at a forest, a field, a building site, the shore or the prayer place, and they take up that work.
They float beside your hand and argue out loud over every tempting bit of mischief.
The opening film plays with its soundtrack and dissolves straight into your island.

releases.title: The Split
releases.summary: Balance, a shadow across the sea, and two very different endings.

items.t: Tend the island and it stays in tune: full colour, birdsong, two rings of gold light in the sky. Ruin it and the colour drains and the music slips out of key. Nothing on screen names it; the island shows you.

items.h: Vexahl is there from day one
items.t: A dark spire far out at sea. As the world tips out of balance it drifts closer. As you mend it, it backs away.
A round orb of light that speaks at the big moments only. It asks, it warns once, it notices. It never tells you what to do.
Totem, then a ring of standing stones, then a pyramid, then a temple, each one rising where your people dance.
Answer a village's prayers and a white star with a long gold tail may cross its sky.
And the island remembers them: the lost child you carried home, the family you saved from a fire.
In one, the world falls quiet and begins again, remembering. The other we won't spoil.

items.h: No words to read while you play
items.t: Prayers are pictures now, and the game teaches through play.
Finish THE PATH and your initials are waiting in the god-name box.

releases.title: THE FIRST WORLD
releases.summary: The game got its name and its mark, and your island can follow you to any device.

items.t: Leave a god name and get a code like AMBER-OTTER-4821. It brings your island back on any device, any time.
New prayers fly into a tidy list at the side; click one to fly to that village.
Grabbing is more forgiving, a soft gold ring shows what you're pointing at, and a glowing mark shows where things will land.

items: The golem no longer gets stuck walking into houses.

releases.title: The living island
items: Villages pray for timber, food, rain, a sign or a lost child brought home. Answer them and their faith grows.
Two little advisors arrive: Lumi, a kind spirit, and Fizz, a cheeky imp.
Four seasons, each with its own weather: spring blossom, a summer dry spell, an autumn storm, a winter cold snap.
A rival god across the sea, with schemes you can always see coming and always counter.
Your island saves itself, so you can pick up where you left off.
Sixteen kinds of tree, a painted landscape, and a brand-new hand.

releases.title: The golem and the soundscape
items: A stone golem to raise. Stroke it, pat it or scold it, and it grows into whoever you taught it to be.
A soundscape where every chime, splash and footstep is in the same key as the music.

releases.title: The first island
items: An island, a sea, a sky that turns from day to night, and a hand that can pick up almost anything.
Villagers who farm, build, raise families and pray. Miracles of water, food and fire.
